$comment: The authoritative WebTransport conformance scenario list. Both runners —
read this file and refuse to start unless they implement exactly these ids,
so a scenario cannot quietly exist on only one side.
handler/query name a path on apps/wpt_server.zig, which mirrors the Python
runners lists who can run it: a browser is left out when the API the
scenario needs does not exist there. Where only some versions have it, the
body reports n/a on the others instead of passing on nothing.
expect_fail records a known failure with its reason, per engine and per
version range, so a red cell is a tracked cell rather than a surprise, on
'N-M' (inclusive), compared part by part: '26.4' and '27' both work.
Engines: chrome, firefox, safari, safari-preview, webkit (Playwright's).

scenarios.title: establish and close a session
client close carries code and reason to the server
exercises: the server's record of the close, read back through query.py

scenarios.title: server close with code 0 and a reason
server close with a non-zero code
server close with the largest code WPT exercises
abrupt QUIC close rejects rather than resolves
echo a short message on a bidirectional stream
three concurrent bidirectional streams stay distinct
64 KB round trip on a bidirectional stream
client uni stream echoed back on a new server uni stream
64 KB on a unidirectional stream
five server uni streams all arrive, whole and distinct

firefox.why: Bug 2046262: the incoming-streams ReadableStream stops pulling while a stream is already queued, so only 2 of the 5 surface. Fixed in 153.

scenarios.title: datagram round trip
maxDatagramSize is positive
a datagram at maxDatagramSize arrives whole

safari.why: Safari 26.4 reports maxDatagramSize as the QUIC max_datagram_frame_size (65535) rather than a path-MTU-derived size, so a datagram of that size is refused by its own stack. Chrome reports 1024 and the Zig client 1199. Technology Preview 27.0 reports 1024; later releases are not measured.

scenarios.title: a server RESET_STREAM surfaces with its application code
a client RESET_STREAM reaches the server with its code
a server STOP_SENDING surfaces with its application code
DRAIN_WEBTRANSPORT_SESSION resolves draining without closing

firefox.why: Firefox 155+ has `draining`, but neqo knows no WT_DRAIN_SESSION and drops it as an unknown capsule: it resolves only on GOAWAY (see server-goaway). 148-154 have no attribute and report n/a.

safari-preview.why: Safari Technology Preview 27.0 never resolves `WebTransport.draining` on a WT_DRAIN_SESSION capsule: the scenario timed out in both clean runs of three, where release 26.4 passed it in all three against the same server.

webkit.why: Playwright's WebKit build 2370 (27.2's engine, on macOS 26.6.2's Network.framework) never resolves `draining` on a WT_DRAIN_SESSION that arrives in the 200's flight; the same capsule once the session is up resolves it (server-goaway). Not on GOAWAY alone.

scenarios.title: GOAWAY with WT_DRAIN_SESSION resolves draining without closing
WT-Available-Protocols offer answered with WT-Protocol

firefox.why: WebTransport.protocol lands in Firefox 155; earlier versions leave it undefined.
